claude.sample_unit: patients with diabetes (47,958 New Zealand; 46,558 Chinese)
models_evaluated: New Zealand sex-specific 5-year CVD risk equations (Cox-based)
New Zealand equations recalibrated to Chinese cohort
New Zealand equations with Chinese age coefficients

links.outcome: Calibration (expected to observed ratio) after recalibration versus updating age coefficients in Chinese cohort
links.effect: Standard recalibration did not improve calibration (E/O 0.938 men, 0.809 women); replacing NZ age coefficients with Chinese ones improved it (E/O 1.027 men, 1.025 women).
links.quote: Replacing New Zealand age coefficients with Chinese coefficients noticeably improved calibration (expected to observed ratio 1.027 in men, 1.025 in women).

links.outcome: Performance of NZ-derived equations when applied to a Chinese population with diabetes
links.effect: Applying the high-income-country equation to a non-high-income population may introduce systematic errors, driven by differing age effects (age HR women 1.61 NZ vs 2.51 China per 10 years).
links.quote: Applying a high income country derived CVD risk prediction equation to a population from a non-high income country with diabetes may introduce systematic errors, primarily driven by differing effect of age.

unlisted_practices: Updating key predictor coefficients (e.g., age) beyond simple recalibration when transporting risk equations across countries

models_evaluated: New Zealand equations with standard recalibration
New Zealand equations with Chinese age coefficients

links.effect: Standard recalibration E:O ratio: 0.938 in men, 0.809 in women.
links.quote: Standard recalibration of New Zealand equations did not improve calibration in the Chinese cohort (expected to observed ratio: 0.938 in men, 0.809 in women).

links.effect: Women age HR: 1.61 (1.51 to 1.71) in New Zealand, 2.51 (2.32 to 2.72) in China.
links.quote: Hazard ratios for most predictors were similar between New Zealand and Chinese equations but differed markedly for age (eg, women: 1.61, 95% confidence interval 1.51 to 1.71 per 10 years in New Zealand, 2.51 (2.32 to 2.72) per 10 years in China).

links.effect: Replacing age coefficients improved E:O ratio to 1.027 in men, 1.025 in women.
links.quote: Replacing New Zealand age coefficients with Chinese coefficients noticeably improved calibration (expected to observed ratio 1.027 in men, 1.025 in women).

links.outcome: calibration of CVD risk prediction equations
links.effect: calibration improved to expected to observed ratio of 1.027 in men and 1.025 in women
links.quote: Replacing New Zealand age coefficients with Chinese coefficients noticeably improved calibration (expected to observed ratio 1.027 in men, 1.025 in women).

screen.reason: The study empirically tests strategies for transporting a risk model from one population to another, comparing standard recalibration versus updating specific predictor coefficients to evaluate model transportability and calibration safeguards.

primary.practice: local recalibration and updating predictor coefficients
